partner_result_applied.result: common product envelope and conditional hyperbolic L3 gate

proved_results: For every q>2, the quadratic oscillatory transform of one arbitrary density-capped input satisfies ||F||_q <= C_q |a|^(-1/q) with explicit C_q.
At q=3, ||F||_3^3 <= 16*pi/|a| and hence an eta-superlevel frequency budget.
The strong L2 endpoint fails for X uniform on [0,1].
Conditioning transfers the same Lq bound to a fully coupled quadratic form whenever a selected original-coordinate diagonal coefficient is nonzero.
Using the partner product envelope, a zero-diagonal off-diagonal pair gives a full-form conditional L3 gate <3.67 |a_ij|^(-1/3).
A three-dimensional indefinite shell gives an exact counterexample to projection-density-only closure while not being a target counterexample because the law is not product.
unresolved_implication: Find a dimension-free aggregation of many small original-coordinate oscillatory gates from the three-large-eigenvalue hypothesis while preserving product structure; single-entry selection loses dimension and bounded spectral-projection density alone is insufficient.
next_step: Combine conditional square and partner hyperbolic atoms with a Cauchy-Binet/minor or decoupling average that sums rather than maximizes coordinate contributions.
